title: Incident triage journal — Taylor (on-call shift)
body:
Shift: 2026-03-18 08:00–16:00 local (PST)
Summary: weird latency spikes hitting hosted-api edge for ~20m around 09:12. Pages escalated by alert: api-99p-latency > 1500ms for 3min.

09:10 — pager -> quick glance
- Alert source: datadog / synthetic check (api-generation-latency-prod).
- Initial hypothesis: sudden autoscaling lag / scheduling or backend queueing.
- Slack: pinged @Maya and #sre-oncall with top-3 spans.

09:15 — triage
- kubectl top pods --namespace=hosted-api -> nodes looked fine (CPU low), bursty request queueing on a few replicas (pod-12, pod-5).
- curl health endpoints on pods: pod-5 returned 200 but response headers show high X-serve-latency.
- Checked runtime logs: repeated KV cache miss flood then long tail tokenization step. Pattern: certain client path /v1/generate?model=llama-2-13b caused heavier KV churn.

Actions taken
- Triggered a temporary routing rule to divert traffic for the offending model tag to dedicated pool (manual via console) at 09:22 — latency normalized within ~4m.
- Rolled forward a canary change rollback (gh PR linked) that had minor kernel selector tweak — rollback seemed correlated but not the root cause.

09:40 — stabilize
- Increased suffix cache TTL for generation prefix cache for 5m as mitigation.
- Noted that autoscaler did not spin up extra pods quickly; config threshold is interlocked with queue depth metric that underreports when KV cache misses spike.

Incidents notes (for postmortem & follow-ups)
- Root cause (proximate): workload pattern (replay of long-context requests) exposed a scheduling + autoscaler config blindspot.
- Suspected secondary contributor: recent kernel selection change increased per-token CPU variability (PR #911).

Runbook TODOs (items to own or hand off)
- Update autoscaler playbook: add KV-miss sensitive metric (queue-depth + kv-miss-rate) as a scaler signal (owner: Taylor, due: 2026-03-20).
- Add a canary gating checklist for kernel selector PRs that includes synthetic long-context load (owner: Applied ML / Runtime team, due: 2026-03-25).
- Create alert: sustained model-specific 95th latency > 1000ms for 2 min (suppress noise by only firing when requests/sec > 5) (owner: Samir).
- Postmortem ticket INFRA-3456 (create draft, include timeline, links to logs/graphs, mitigation steps).

Commands & quick artifacts (copied)
- kubectl -n hosted-api get pods -o wide | grep pod-5
- kubectl logs pod-5 -c runtime --since=30m | grep "kv miss"
- datadog query: avg:trace.duration{service:hosted-api,env:prod}.rollup(avg, 60) by {resource} > 1000

Open questions / notes to self
- Why did autoscaler prioritise CPU signals over queue-depth? Check HPA config and the custom metrics adapter mapping.
- Is there a way to pre-warm KV cache for long-context models at route time? Talk to runtime team about eager prefix caching.
- Investigate whether the canary that landed last night actually hit only canary nodes or leaked to prod routing. Follow up with release-engineering.

Follow-ups for tomorrow
- Sync 30m with runtime eng to review PR #911 behavior under long-context synthetic. (Add calendar invite)
- Draft runbook update and send to eng-sre for review.
- Compile a short ops-note (2–3 bullets) for upstream prod chat summarizing mitigation and next steps.

Personal bookmarks / reminders
- Look into adding a tiny script to fetch top offending paths from traces regularly and dump to /tmp when alerts fire. Might help fast triage.
- Remember to mute noisy synthetic in datadog temporarily if we add new filters.

Shift end checklist
- File a short summary in INFRA-3456 ticket and assign to Samir for alerts work.
- Drop post-incident note in #prod-ops with links and a rough timeline.
- Mark runbook TODOs in the playbook repo as issues.

Misc (handy paste for handover)
- Short timeline: 09:12 alert -> 09:22 reroute -> 09:26 latency normalized -> 09:40 mitigation TTL bump -> ongoing follow-up.
- If paging for same signature appears, immediately route model-tag to dedicated pool and notify runtime team.

End of entry — T.N.
